Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press the pound key. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Group's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Thomas Greer, Chief Operating Officer; Amanda Ruiz, Chief Marketing Officer; and Kevin Walsh, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Group delivered record results in the Q3 2024, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. On revenue diversification, we've shifted significantly toward fee-based streams, with non-interest income now at 39% of total revenue, buffering against NIM pressures. Market conditions boosted non-interest income through strong investment banking fees and wealth management inflows despite volatility. For loan growth and credit quality, we expect 5-7% growth with stable metrics like NPLs at 78 bps. Fee income across wealth management, investment banking, and cards grew robustly, driven by AUM expansion and payment volumes. NII expanded to 3.52%, with Q4 guidance pointing higher. Provisions reflect disciplined CECL modeling amid portfolio growth. Deposit costs rose modestly to 2.72% under competitive pressures, but our beta remains low. Finally, credit metrics show improving trends, with NCOs at 42 bps and strong coverage.

I will now turn the call over to David Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

David Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning. Apex Financial Group reported net income of $2.8 billion for the Q3 2024, or $2.45 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8% year-over-year, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 14% year-over-year, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Let me dive deeper into our revenue diversification initiatives, which have been central to our strategic transformation over the past two years. In a landscape of persistent inflation, higher-for-longer rates, and regulatory challenges like Basel IV, we've moved our revenue mix from traditional NII toward resilient fee streams. This enhances earnings stability, boosts ROE, and positions us in growth areas. Total revenue hit $12.4 billion, up 8% YoY, with non-interest revenue expanding 15% to $4.8 billion—now 39% of the mix, ahead of our 35% target and up from 28% two years ago. This cushioned a 2 bps NIM contraction to 3.12% as deposit betas normalized with Fed funds at 5.25-5.50%, delivering 22% pre-provision operating ROE versus mid-teens for NII-heavy peers.

Our efforts span wealth and asset management, transaction banking and payments, capital markets, and digital ecosystems. In wealth and asset management, our One Wealth platform integrates brokerage, advisory, and alternatives for mass-affluent clients, pushing AUM to $1.2 trillion, up 18% YoY on 12% net new flows including $45 billion into ESG and private credit amid 4.5% 10-year Treasury yields. Fees jumped 25% to $1.9 billion at 42 bps, with cross-sell to 28% of our 15 million consumer clients. U.S. grew 22%, APAC via HSBC heritage added $150 billion from HNW in Singapore and Hong Kong with Sharia products.

Transaction banking and payments surged 32% to $1.6 billion, 13% of revenue, via $500 million Global PayHub investment for real-time cross-border and embedded finance with Visa Direct and Plaid. Trade volumes up 28% to $450 billion, DACH TBI fees up 40% post-Brexit, payments SaaS ARR at $800 million with 85% margins, onboarding 5,000 SMEs on PSD3-compliant APIs.

Capital markets and investment banking fees rose 19% to $1.1 billion despite 15% M&A drop, leaning into ECM and lev-fin with $120 billion bonds, 25% advisory growth in energy transition, top-5 in green bonds, LatAm DCM doubled on commodities.

Digital ecosystems like Pinnacle Go neobank with 8 million users added $300 million interchange up 50% via BNPL, plus $400 million structured deposits and auto-leasing fees at 150 bps, low delinquencies from 92% accurate ML scoring.

Enablers include data/AI Lakehouse processing 10 petabytes for 15% wallet share lift, embedded partnerships beyond Visa/Mastercard, and regulatory navigation under Dodd-Frank. Volatility down 30%, CET1 at 12.8%, P/E up 1.2x peers. We see non-interest at 42% by 2025, $2-3 billion incremental ARR.

Turning to the impact of market conditions on non-interest income, which totaled $2.55 billion, up 14% YoY and 28% of revenue—strongest since Q4 2021. This shows diversification amid Fed terminal rates at 5.25-5.50%, 2.5% CPI, S&P up 22% YTD but Russell 2000 at 8%.

Investment banking fees at $825 million, +28% YoY, from 35% IPO surge to $45 billion, 4.2% ECM share via Bloomberg EMSX, M&A advisory +22% on $180 billion volume including pharma deals, though DCM +5% on 420 bps HY spreads. Americas 65%, APAC 20% on China stimulus, EMEA 15%.

Markets revenue $620 million, -3% YoY, from low VIX at 15.5 crimping FICC -8% to $380 million amid curve steepening, equities flat at $240 million on options, CVAs/DVAs +$15 million. AI with Palantir improved TCA by 2.5 bps.

Asset management/wealth $510 million +12%, AUM $1.8 trillion on $120 billion inflows, 42 bps fees resilient vs. ETF wars, alternatives at 15% portfolios yielding 9%. US +15%, APAC +18%, EMEA flat post-UBS.

Cards/payments/service $420 million +9%, volumes $450 billion +16% at 2.1% interchange post-Durbin, overdraft/NSF -5% offset by Plaid, treasury +12%.

Other $175 million +2%. Fees cover 65% expenses, hedging NIM at 3.45%. Initiatives: Stripe embedded finance for $500 million run-rate, Ion blockchain for 40% faster trade, AI fraud cuts 25%. Guide 10-12% growth FY25 on cuts, S&P 6000, $4T M&A.

On fee income breakdown, fees grew 14% YoY to $2.8 billion, 42% of revenue up from 38%, exceeding 10-12% guide, core +12% ex-$150 million gain. Favorable mix to advisory/transactional.

Wealth management $1.35 billion +18%, 48% of fees, AUM $1.9 trillion +11% organic. Equities +9% added $120 billion, NNM $45 billion record, Wealth 360 AI up advisor productivity 25%, cross-sell to 22%. Fee rate 65 bps, alternatives/ESG 15% at 90 bps. NA 60%, APAC +32%, EMEA countered non-dom with UCITS. Wealth Everywhere robo in app, 1.2 million digital, +15% cross-sell. FY25 12-15%.

Investment banking $750 million +9%, #4 M&A, M&A advisory $340 million +22% on 15 megadeals like tech/energy. ECM -5% $180 million, DCM +35% $230 million on IG/green bonds. Americas 55%, APAC 15%, EMEA 20%. IBX blockchain -40% execution. 8-11% growth, ROE 25%+.

Cards $700 million +16%, GPV $450 billion +13%, premium Black Card 2.5 million 40% fees at 2.8% interchange. Late/over $120 million +5%, co-brand $80 million, digital wallet 35%. US 70%, EM +25% BNPL. ML fraud -22% chargebacks. Target 20% households.

Fee 3.0: digitize for 20% efficiency, premiumize for $84T transfer, ESG 12%. FY 13-15% growth.

NII was $1.28 billion +8% YoY +3% QoQ, beating consensus, NIM 3.52% +5 bps, > peers. Earning assets $185 billion +4%, loans $142 billion +6%, C&I +9% at 6.8%, CRE flat 5.9%, consumer +5% 5.2%. Deposits $168 billion +7%, core 42%, beta 65%, cost 1.85% +2 bps. L/D 84%, $25 billion liquidity.

Southeast +12% NII. Aladdin hedges $12 billion securities, AI pricing +15 bps spreads, wealth $45 billion AUM +$120 million fees.

Q4 NII $1.30-1.34 billion, NIM 3.55-3.60%, loans +1-2%, deposits stable. EPS $1.55-1.65, ROTE 14.5-15.2%, prov $180-200 million, CET1 11.2%.

Provisions for credit losses at $625 million +15% QoQ -8% YoY, NCO 52 bps stable, ACL 1.45% or $12.4 billion, 3.2x NCOs. CECL PD/LGD/EAD with 20+ years data, Moody's/S&P, IRB PIT via Fed scenarios.

Consumer 42% book $280 million prov, +7% growth, delinq 2.8%, subprime auto LGD 55%. C&I 35% $220 million, util 48%, PD 1.2%. CRE 18% $105 million +25% QoQ, office vac 19.5%, multi 4.2% cap. Mort/HELOC $20 million.

Base GDP 2.1% unemp 4.3%, adverse 25% weight unemp 5.5%. US 85%, Europe flat, APAC low PD. XGBoost ML +15% accuracy, alt data, +$75 million overlays, recoveries 45%.

Tighten subprime auto 15%, CRE office -20%, Q3 PCL $600-650 million.

Cost of deposits averaged 2.72% +18 bps QoQ +112 bps YoY, deposits $285 billion +4% QoQ +12% YoY. NIBD 0.05% 28%, NOW/MM 2.45% 42%, savings/CDs 3.12%, comm/brokered 4.18% 15%. Beta 42% IBD < peers.

Competition: liquidity flush, Ally/SoFi 4.20-4.50%, CDs 4.85%. Midwest moderate, coasts fierce. NIM 3.42% -16 bps, 65% from deposits.

Dynamic pricing Q2/Finastra retains 85% CDs, Rewards tiers 3.75%, digital +28% -15 bps, tokenized pilots, FHLB $4.5 billion 4.10%. Q3 2.85-2.90%, FY 2.65%, NIM 3.55% on cuts. L/D 92%.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, David. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, geopolitical tensions, commercial real estate stress, and cyber threats. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, including macro hedging with VaR at $25 million and Basel IV IRB floors.

Robert Kline:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with NPL ratio at 78 basis points, down 12 bps QoQ, net charge-offs at 42 bps annualized up slightly from 39 bps but below peers, and delinquencies improving to 1.45% early-stage. Trends show C&I NPLs 45 bps, CRE 112 bps with office at 2.8%, consumer stable. NCOs ex-one-time 35 bps, ACL 1.28% or 286% NPL coverage. Southeast outperforms at 65 bps NPLs. ML platform +22% prediction, collections 92%. Expect NPLs low-80s, NCOs 40 bps.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI-driven underwriting and cloud-native platforms like Lakehouse and Global PayHub are yielding significant results, processing petabytes for personalization, reducing decision times 40%, and boosting fraud detection.

Thomas Greer:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making, targeting efficiency ratio under 58%.

Amanda Ruiz:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention, with Wealth Everywhere and Rewards programs lifting cross-sell 15% and digital users.

Kevin Walsh:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements, including PSD3, SFDR, and Dodd-Frank stress tests.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Jennifer Hale with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Hale:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on revenue diversification initiatives?

Michael Reynolds:
Thanks, Jennifer. As David outlined, our shift to 39% non-interest mix via wealth, payments, CIB, and digital has de-risked earnings—volatility down 30%, ROE up—with AUM $1.2T, PayHub ARR $800M, and neobank growth. We're on track for 42% by 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson:
What is your outlook for NII and earnings next quarter?

David Chen:
Mark, Q4 NII $1.30-1.34B at 3.55-3.60% NIM on steady Fed, loan/deposit growth. EPS $1.55-1.65, prov 25-30 bps, supported by hedges and pricing engines.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Can you discuss the impact of credit risks in CRE?

Lisa Patel:
Emily, CRE is 28% of loans, selective in multi/industrial, office pulled back 12%. Criticized 2.1%, reserves 120%, stress-tested CET1 >11.5% severe recession. Proactive monitoring up 15% in Sunbelt.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
What are your plans for technology in loan growth?

Elena Vasquez:
David, cloud decisioning cut times 40%, ML scoring 92% accurate for $500M underserved growth like green finance. Complements 5-7% loan outlook with quality.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Michael Reynolds for any closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
